items.title: Gacha Games takeover ANIME Impulse Orange County
items.summary: Chinese and Korean games carve out a larger space in the anime community.
items.content:
On Aug. 22-23, ANIME Impulse Orange County was held at the Anaheim Convention Center alongside K-PLAY! Fest and Collector Expo.

ANIME Impulse is an anime, manga and fandom convention that is primarily hosted in California. The convention is known for its large vendor halls, artist alley, voice actor guests and DEKOCAR Itasha showcases (heavily decorated anime-themed cars).

This year, ANIME Impulse Orange County has been officially sponsored by three major gacha games from China and South Korea: “Zenless Zone Zero” (also known as ZZZ), “Honkai: Star Rail” and “GODDESS OF VICTORY: NIKKE.”

The term “Gacha games” refers to a video game mechanic where players can summon characters, accessories and different items with in-game currency through a luck-based system. “Gacha” also refers to small toy vending machines in Japan, “Gachapon.”

Gacha games have traditionally had a strong presence in anime conventions. Many gacha games from Japan were multimedia projects, having their own anime, multiple games and sequels that are frequently being promoted at conventions.

Gacha game fans also overlapped with regular anime fans. Popular examples from Japan include “Fate/Grand Order” and “Granblue Fantasy,” which both have been featured in different anime cons such as Anime Expo and Anime NYC.

Each game sponsor was represented by several merchandise booths and activities made for fans and anyone curious about the game. Their presence in the convention scene has shown the fast-growing influence of anime games and anime-adjacent media that originate outside of Japan.

“I think these games definitely deserve more attention,” said Tyler Desotel, a “Zenless Zone Zero” fan. After all, this is how they garner all their attention by doing these crazy things. And I think the fans really do get a lot, even though I haven’t been in it that long.”

The convention had several booths for the three gacha game sponsors selling official or exclusive merchandise, but they were also offering different experiences for attendees to participate in the worlds of the games. The “NIKKE” booth featured a section for attendees to meet, interact and take pictures with official cosplayers who were all in-character.

The “Zenless Zone Zero” area also had a photo-op area with official cosplayers, Itasha cars and a stamp card rally for carnival-style games they had set up for fans to win merchandise of their favorite ZZZ characters.

The area with the carnival games was called the “Proxy Fairgrounds.” Attendees could purchase a $5 ticket to play a game to win character cards and receive a stamp from different ZZZ factions on their card. ZZZ also had a schedule for its official cosplayers’ appearances and even a live concert.

It was not until 2020 that games from outside of Japan started to gain popularity. In September 2020, developer miHoYo released “Genshin Impact” worldwide on multiple platforms, including mobile devices, which made these games very accessible.

On September 28, 2020, Genshin Impact’s X account announced the game reached 10 million pre-registrations and celebrated with an in-game reward for all players. According to GameDaily.biz , Genshin Impact had over 23 million downloads within its first week in app stores.

miHoYo also developed “Honkai: Star Rail” and “Zenless Zone Zero.” These games are known for their expansive open-world gameplay, large casts of characters and frequent updates.

items.title: Petit Planet, Hoyoverse’s Own Spin On The Life Simulation Genre, Launches Winter 2026
China flexes at GamesCom
items.summary: At Opening Night Live’s big trailer showcase today, it seemed like every other game on display was made in China
items.content:
Stephen Totilo Aug 25, 2026 40 2 3 Share A two-hour showcase for upcoming games in Germany today may have ended with segments dedicated to works from top studios in Japan (Final Fantasy VII Retribution out next spring) and Poland (A remaster of Witcher 3 out September 29; an expansion out next year). But it was Chinese game studios that showed up the most.

Opening the show was Nodusfall , a newly revealed co-op action game from Hoyoverse, part of Shanghai-based miHoYo (see trailer above). The new game trades the anime art style used in the company’s Genshin Impact and Honkai Star Rail games for a darker, detailed dark fantasy look, more akin to FromSoftware’s Elden Ring.

Hoyoverse also showed a new trailer for cozy Animal Crossing style game Petit Planet .

Early in the Opening Night Live showcase came a January 15 release date reveal for Ananta , an open-world city-based action game from Hangzhou-based Naked Rain, a subsidiary of Chinese giant NetEase. The hook for this one is that you play as a world-saving social media influencer.

ONL also featured Tides of Annihilation , an upcoming PC, PS5, Xbox action-adventure game involving a ruined London and Arthurian legend, from Chengdu-based Eclipse Glow Games.

From Shanghai-based TiGames came a trailer for Zoopunk , a co-op action game featuring armored anthropomorphized rhinos and chipmunks battling robots. TiGames’ prior release, 2021’s F.I.S.T., had been part of PlayStation’s China Hero Project , an effort to incubate Chinese studios and help them transition into console development.

Chinese studio Hoothanes showed a new trailer for The Defiant , a first-person shooter set on Chinese battlefields during World War II.

The wildest Chinese game shown? Probably Showa American Story , from Wuhan-based Nekcom. The game, per a press release, is a “post-apocalyptic RPG set in an alternate 1980s, [in which] Japan has bought out most of the United States, transforming it into a familiar-yet-strangely-unique backdrop to a zombie outbreak.”

If that wasn’t enough of a trend, even Ubisoft’s reveal of a 2027 console/PC remake for Heroes of Might and Magic III had a Chinese twist. The Paris-headquartered company said the remake’s development is being led by Ubisoft’s China studios in Chengdu and Shanghai.

(And there were more: Aniimo from Hangzhou-based Paw Print, Genigods: Nezha from Genigods Lab, Roco Kingdom from Shenzen-based, Tencent-owned Morefun, Sea of Remnants from Guangzhou-based, NetEase-owned Joker Studio)

Chinese studios aren’t a monolith, aren’t sticking to one genre (we’ve got fantasy action, sure, but also a WWII shooter!), nor one visual style. And they’ve gone well beyond sticking to mobile, with most of these games lined up for some combo of PC and console. Key context to this is that the Chinese-backed games shown were developed by China-based studios; as opposed to coming from the many western studios that the likes of Tencent and NetEase set up in the past several years only to then start shutting down or selling off, bit by bit .

Ubisoft’s Rainbow 6 Tactics is a 2027-slated top-down tactics game (read: kinda like XCOM)

Pony Island 2: Panda Circus , from Inscryption developer Daniel Mullins, got an incredible genre-mash-up trailer and an April 27 2027 release date.

Paradox Interactive’s next grand strategy game is Afterworld , a game about tribes of people trying to survive and rebuild in post-apocalyptic North America. (Paradox is also publishing a Lego-based city-building game, Lego Skylines ).

During the event, miHoYo (HoYoverse) confirmed that HSR would receive a collaboration with another game from the studio – Zenless Zone Zero.

The developers published a small teaser image on social media, a Russian version is also available:

Friends from the world of that game will join our cosmic exploration adventure! Источник изображения: miHoYo (HoYoverse) So far, HSR developers have not revealed the details of this collaboration. They only announced that the joint event between Honkai: Star Rail and Zenless Zone Zero will begin "winter 2026" – without a specific release date for the update.

Earlier this year, miHoYo confirmed the collaboration between Zenless Zone Zero and Honkai: Star Rail. "Winter 2026" was also indicated as the release date.

Insiders reported that some characters from Zenless Zone Zero might appear in Honkai Star Rail, for example, Astra Yao and Ellen Jo were mentioned. It is not yet clear whether they will simply be guest NPCs, or if they will be full-fledged playable characters.

items.title: Honkai: Nexus Anima is a fun creature collector with an incomprehensible story
items.summary: Honkai: Nexus Anima spins off with creature collecting auto-battling gameplay, making for a fun change of pace, though it doesn't quite fit the story.
items.content:
It’s a big deal whenever HoYoverse launches a new game. While it’s true that a new gacha game pops up almost every day, those same gacha games are almost all lifting references or mechanics wholesale from HoYoverse titles. Genshin Impact put the company on the map and shaped what modern gacha games are, and they’ve followed up that hit with Honkai: Star Rail and Zenless Zone Zero, each one making waves and shaking up the industry just a little bit more. It’s safe to assume that HoYoverse wants that same kind of impact from their next major title, and Honkai: Nexus Anima is certainly shaping up to be a swing in a wild new direction. Unfortunately, it’s a big swing that doesn’t fully connect at this time.

Honkai: Nexus Anima is a pretty unique mix of genres and gameplay hooks. While it’s built around creature collecting and will naturally draw comparisons to Pokémon, you aren’t then taking these monsters into turn-based 1v1 battles. Instead, you use them to dive into Teamfight Tactics-style auto battles between big teams of Anima – the creature name in this world.

I’ve always been curious about these sort of idle-battler games, but never met one that hooked me. Using that formula within the context of an anime gacha game, plus mixing in tons of cute collectable creatures, totally does it for me. At first, the depth of combat doesn’t feel particularly vast. There certainly isn’t a high skill ceiling to this style of battle, even as you start mixing in numerous abilities from your Eidos companions. It’s still satisfying to play, but there is a lack of mechanical difficulty at this stage which would need to ramp up to make for a truly satisfying and absorbing endgame.

Outside of battles, Honkai: Nexus Anima will be pretty familiar to you if you’ve dabbled in HoYoverse games. The tutorial section has you exploring some small interactive maps as your chosen protagonist, feeling pretty similar to the small zones of Zenless Zone Zero or Honkai: Star Rail. When you get into the meat of the game, though, you’re tossed into a pretty rich and wide map that combines the scale of a Genshin Impact region with modern buildings and whimsical fantasy meadows.

The game is beautiful, the map is beautiful, the characters you meet are beautiful…but I don’t quite know how to describe them. There isn’t a very clear genre or style to attach Honkai: Nexus Anima to – the other games in the Honkai line were always melting pots of influence that lean heavily toward sci-fi, and Genshin Impact feels similar with a further lean towards Japanese high-fantasy. Honkai: Nexus Anime is bright and bubbly, but impossible to place in the same way.

The story, meanwhile, is not bright or bubbly, but it’s certainly equally incomprehensible. HoYoverse games have an habit of repeating the same two-hit combo in their stories of giving you an amnesiac protagonist, and tossing you into a multidimensional, intergalactic story full of multiple tiers of entities and shadowy realms and world-ending threats and confusing proper nouns. Honkai: Nexus Anima lays it on as thick as usual, with all the gravitas of a grim sci-fi epic. This is a cutesy creature collector, though. The music is whimsical, and the menus are bubbly, but there’s a disconnect between the vibe the game seems to be cultivating and the vibe the story itself is doing. The dense multi-dimensional gacha stories are an acquired taste to start with, but it’s especially egregious here, and I didn’t feel an investment in or understanding of the world I’m exploring because of it.

And that’s a shame, because it really is so much fun to explore this world. Each Anima you bond with can be summoned outside of battles to wander around with you and bust out their unique abilities. One type can smash through walls, while another can become a hilarious improvised trampoline for you to bounce off. I was pretty addicted to the gameplay loop I found myself in, where I’d spend time exploring the world to find new Anima, then I’d dive into battles to see which ones fit together best in a team. And then, once I found a team I liked, I could set out to keep training and uncapping my favourite Anima to make them as strong as possible.

It’s so much fun to play Honkai: Nexus Anima and it’s take on the creature collecting genre, but from the closed beta test, that gets lost in the bland world and incomprehensible story. Being invested in the characters and the story is my biggest reason for picking up a gacha game, and without that, I already have one foot out the door with Honkai: Nexus Anima. I’m hopeful that, as we head towards the full release, HoYoverse can massage these problems and reel me back in.

items.title: "Honkai: Star Rail Version 4.2 "So Laughed the Masses" will arrive on April 22"
items.summary: The Path of Elation awaits when Version 4.2 'So Laughed the Masses' launches on April 22nd.
items.content:
SINGAPORE, April 10, 2026 — Global interactive entertainment brand HoYoverse announced today that Honkai: Star Rail's new Version 4.2, "So Laughed the Masses," will officially launch on April 22. With the rewards of Phantasmoon Games receiving a massive escalation, more eyes across the universe will converge on Planarcadia, and the intensity of the competition will greatly increase. Embrace the new power of the Path of Elation, and march towards final victory alongside Silver Wolf LV.999, who has completed her ascension, and the observer Evanescia! Click to watch the latest trailer: https://youtu.be/NyM_seY0XKg

Click here to obtain the media kit: https://hoyoverse.box.com/s/u3ej6hdz0s88q3x75qkx8kr5f5fy3ewb Meanwhile, to celebrate the upcoming third anniversary of Honkai: Star Rail, the game has meticulously prepared a series of special events and generous rewards, inviting players to join in on the fun. In Version 4.2, the anniversary-exclusive event "Festive Gifts" will make its return, allowing players to check in and receive a total of 20 pulls. Also returning is another highly anticipated player tradition: on the anniversary day of April 26, Trailblazers can select a blessing card from a companion and receive a special gift of 1,600 Stellar Jades. Not to mention, the third-anniversary birthday surprises are an absolute must-see: the limited 5-star characters Huohuo and Robin will be added to the "Stellar Convergence" Store. As is tradition, Trailblazers can use a freely claimed Golden Companion Spirit to exchange for their companion of choice in the store. Furthermore, in addition to the annual first-time top-up double bonus reset, there's even more content waiting for players to explore, including new arrivals in the Gift of Stardust Store and a new Outfit for Castorice! As the anniversary celebration approaches, participate in the "Aha's Chosen: Spreading Elation Everywhere" online event and leave your message for a chance to win multiple grand prizes, including a "Crown of Aha" Silver Wolf LV.999-themed car. At the same time, global cities such as Tokyo, Seoul, and Los Angeles will progressively launch a series of online and offline celebration activities, including themed parades, street festivities, and brand collaborations. For more details, please visit the official website: https://hoyo.link/GXrf0ZdtR In the Version 4.2 Main Story, the stakes of the Phantasmoon Games become a whole lot more complicated once it's announced that the ultimate reward has received an unprecedented escalation: the victor will become the permanent Aeon of Elation. Caught right in the center of the spotlight, the Trailblazer naturally draws the scrutiny and wariness of every major faction. At that moment, Fulwish — leader of the Research Society of Happy Smiles and a local media mogul — invited all Supplicants to the Fulwish TV headquarters in Seafeld City, a holiday resort renowned for its crisp scenery and idyllic climate. There, Fulwish plans to host a televised debate open to all of arcadia, exploring the burning question: "What kind of future will the Phantasmoon Games bring to this world?" For the Trailblazer, this "public provocation" is undoubtedly an overt scheme that is impossible to refuse. And beneath the surface of the debate lurks a myriad of traps and tricks. Pitted against Fulwish, a master at swaying minds and inciting public opinion, can the Trailblazer navigate every hurdle, gather more Wishpower, and resolve the hidden crisis? Meanwhile, fellow Supplicants Silver Wolf and Pearl have struck a mysterious deal that might just be the key to turning the tide of battle. With the competition heating up, two brand-new 5-star characters Silver Wolf LV.999 and Evanescia will officially join the team, becoming crucial companions to help the Trailblazer turn the tables. First up, a familiar face: Silver Wolf is making her grand entrance with a brand-new look. As a long-time member of the Stellaron Hunters, she needs no introduction. If you had to pick the universe's most hardcore gamer, Silver Wolf takes the crown, hands down. If you treat the vast universe as a game of endless level ups and progress, then "Silver Wolf LV.999" is what happens when she hits level 999 and evolves into a "Godmode Player." This hacker from Punklorde also happens to be the very first Emanator of the Elation from the Phantasmoon Games to step into the spotlight. Silver Wolf LV.999 is a 5-star Imaginary character following the Path of Elation. In combat, she can rack up "Hidden MMR" to activate her exclusive Cartridge and enter the "Godmode Player" state. Once active, Silver Wolf pulls both teammates and enemies alike into her own gaming domain, unlocking a "Reward stage" at the start of her turn. During this "Reward stage," she can use her Cartridge to spawn various in-game items, not only shaking up the combat dynamics but also sharing powerful buffs with teammates to turn the tide together. When "Aha Instant" strikes, Silver Wolf blasts all enemies with a game-crashing laser cannon, dealing massive DMG. On top of that, this hacker from Punklorde has one more trick up her sleeve: when a teammate falls under enemy control, she'll hack into the battlefield — even if she isn't actively in the team — granting allies temporary immunity to control. It's her own special way of keeping the team protected during every battle. Next up is Evanescia. Since the start of the Phantasmoon Games, this mysterious girl has always been watching this game's progress as an observer. In fact, as a "Special Observer," Evanescia has participated in far more than just one iteration of the Phantasmoon Games. Because of this, this multi-playthrough player has already witnessed way too many contestants scheming against one another to fight for Wishpower, and watched countless people repeatedly clash on the heels of Aeonic power. Rather than looking forward to who will become the ultimate champion of the Phantasmoon Games, she pays much more attention to the performance of her favored "protagonist": the Trailblazer. And in the new story, more secrets regarding Evanescia's true identity will also gradually reach a final revelation. Evanescia is a 5-star Physical character following the Path of Elation. In combat, Evanescia can continuously accumulate "Certified Banger" through various means: whether she regenerates Energy, teammates Charge her, or the "Certified Banger" on her teammates changes, she continues to gain "Certified Banger." Whenever Evanescia gains "Certified Banger," she will simultaneously regenerate Energy, allowing her to maintain her DMG rhythm. As "Certified Banger" continues to accumulate, Evanescia's DMG will also gradually increase. Whenever it reaches a certain number of points, it will additionally trigger an attack from "Master Fox," dealing DMG to all enemies and regenerating Energy for Evanescia. Her Elation Skill can also attack all enemies. While delivering a stylish performance, it will further increase the team's overall DMG. In addition to the two highly anticipated new characters, the Trailblazer on the Path of Elation will also join the team in Version 4.2. As the Elation Trailblazer's brand-new weapon, the glow stick features a rich variety of uses. When using their Skill, the glow stick transforms into a lightblade as the Trailblazer deals DMG to all enemies and gains "Certified Banger". Not only that, the glow stick can also turn into nunchucks, unleashing a spectacular flurry of attacks on surrounding enemies and dealing multiple instances of DMG. Beyond that, it can also be used to hype up teammates. When using their Ultimate, the Trailblazer can select a teammate to cheer for. This allows the chosen teammate to gain "Certified Banger" while immediately using their Elation Skill, paving the way for an even more lively combat experience! Additionally, a special Warp event will kick off in the first half of Version 4.2. Limited 5-star characters The Dahlia, Castorice, and Firefly will be getting a rerun. Meanwhile, in the Warp event for the second half, limited 5-star characters Tribbie, Sunday, and Feixiao will also have their reruns. On top of that, four existing characters — Firefly, Huohuo, Seele, and Welt — will all be receiving buffs, continuing to provide indispensable help for players on their trailblazing expedition. Finally, right in time for the 3rd Anniversary of Honkai: Star Rail, a host of exciting events will be arriving alongside the grand festivities. In Version 4.2, the brand-new event "Cosmic Data Roaming" will officially go live, allowing Trailblazers to build a top-tier streamer career by broadcasting their sleekest combat moments. Following the version update, Currency Wars will also receive a massive expansion, offering Trailblazers more diverse gameplay options. Meanwhile, the Cosmicon Collective is bringing the heat with its Version 2.0 update, "Cosmicon, Roll On Again!," introducing not only new decks and dice, but also a brand-new team challenge gameplay mode. In addition, exciting events and features like "Express Renovation Escapade" and "Relic Recon" will also be rolling out to help Trailblazers fully enjoy the anniversary fun. At the end of this Special Program, the original animation project co-produced by HoYoverse and MAPPA premiered its concept trailer, "Death in the Afternoon." Please look forward to the continuing cosmic adventures! Honkai: Star Rail is now available on PC, iOS, Android, Epic Games Store, and PS5, and has exceeded 150 million total downloads across all platforms. In 2023, the game won Apple's App Store iPhone Game of the Year, Google Play's Best Game, and BEST MOBILE GAME by The Game Awards. In 2024, it received the Golden Joystick Awards Still Playing Award (Mobile) and PlayStation® Partner Awards 2024 PARTNER AWARD among other honors. The game has been rated Teen by the ESRB and is also classified as PEGI 12. If you wish to learn more details, please visit https://hsr.hoyoverse.com or follow @HonkaiStarRail on Twitter (X), Instagram, and Facebook. About Honkai: Star Rail Honkai: Star Rail is a space fantasy RPG title with a journey through immense worlds of the unknown. The player takes on the role of "Trailblazer," a courageous individual implanted with a powerful artifact, Stellaron, and bearing the determination to unravel the mysteries surrounding the fabled "Cancer of All Worlds" and Aeons. The game features fantasy elements with myths and legends integrated into the space sci-fi story. Combined with the intuitive turn-based combat system, diverse and distinctive companions, and immersive storylines that together compose an interstellar melody filled with captivating worlds, each brimming with unique cultures, awe-inspiring landscapes, and mythical wonders to explore. About HoYoverse HoYoverse is committed to providing immersive virtual world experiences to players around the world. We have brought fans popular games including Genshin Impact, Honkai: Star Rail, Honkai Impact 3rd, Tears of Themis, and Zenless Zone Zero, as well as a wide range of entertainment content. Community is at the heart of everything we do. We are devoted to engaging fans and fostering an enthusiastic and inclusive global community that provides access and encouragement for people to share their passion for ACG (Animation, Comics, and Games) through their own creativity and skills. Pushing the boundaries of imagination, we consistently explore cutting-edge game development technologies, and have accumulated leading technical capabilities in cel shading, cloud gaming, and other fields. In the future, we will continue to expand our content production, technology research, and publishing duties through operations in offices in Singapore, Montreal, Los Angeles, Tokyo, Seoul, and other areas. items.title: MAPPA, HoYoverse Release 'Animation Concept Trailer' for Honkai: Star Rail Game (Updated)
items.content:
HoYoverse revealed during a livestream for its Honkai: Star Rail game on Friday that it and MAPPA have co-produced an "animation concept trailer" for the game. The trailer, viewable below, is titled "Death in the Afternoon."

Yuzuru Tachikawa ( Mob Psycho 100 , Death Parade director) directed the trailer and Kayoko Ishikawa ( Sarazanmai , ZENSHU. ) was the character designer. The end of the above video features the words " MAPPA Honkai: Star Rail Animation A New Story Awaits."

The HoYoverse staff had introduced the video in the livestream as a "mysterious collaboration project." HoYoverse's press release about the livestream announcements stated that at the end of the livestream, "...the original animation project co-produced by HoYoverse and MAPPA premiered its concept trailer, 'Death in the Afternoon.' Please look forward to the continuing cosmic adventures!"

The livestream and HoYoverse's press release did not give any further details. It is currently unclear if the "original animation project" is the above trailer, or if the collaboration will include other works.

Update: ANN reached out to HoYoverse for clarification, and the company provided the following response:

HoYoverse launched its Honkai: Star Rail game for PC and mobile in April 2023, and then for PlayStation 5 in October 2023. The game has exceeded 150 million total downloads across all platforms.

The game will launch its Version 4.2 patch on April 22. The patch will celebrate the game's third anniversary.

HoYoverse's earlier game Genshin Impact launched a "long-term collaboration project" with ufotable in 2022. The project is still in production.

Sources: Press release, Honkai: Star Rail game's YouTube channel ( link 2 )

items.title: We Were All Wrong About Honkai Star Rail 4.0
Honkai Star Rail is getting a collectible card game in the Version 4.0 update so I guess my life is over now
items.content:
When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works .

(Image credit: Hoyoverse) {alert('Link copied')}).catch(err => {console.error('Failed to copy: ', err)})" data-platform="copy_link" data-action="" class="font-ui-heading py-2 text-sm text-neutral-700 hover:bg-neutral-100 transition-colors no-underline block cursor-pointer border-0 bg-transparent w-full text-left normal-case" aria-label="Copy link" role="menuitem" data-analytics-id="article-social" analytics-label="utility-bar-social-share-copy-link" analytics-name="utility-bar-secondary" data-mrf-recirculation="article-social"> Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Threads Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Honkai: Star Rail Version 4. 0 launches on February 13 The update adds a new planet, new characters, a CCG, and new events Plus, the chance to get a free limited five-star character and 1,600 Stellar Jade Oh no, they've done it now: a collectible card game is coming to Honkai Star Rail in the upcoming 4.0 update.

Sure, there are two new playable characters, a handful of new or expanded events, a generous amount of freebies, and an entire new planet to explore – but I know where I'm really about to lose all of my gaming time.

Before I get lost in the excitement of another game where you collect digital trading cards, let me cover the real key updates that are on the way in Version 4.0, 'No Aha At Full Moon', when it launches on February 13.

So, the characters. Joining the game when the update launches is Yao Guang, a five-star Physical character on the new path of Elation. As a support, she makes allies deals Elation damage, and is all about causing additional triggers of the new Aha Instants mechanic that causes other Elation characters to activate specific skills. A pretty vital piece, then, if you're building a team around the new path.

Following her at the start of March is Sparxie, a five-star Fire character who is also on the Elation path. As a damage dealer, she's the perfect partner to Yao Guang, with the ability to boost your team's critical damage and unleash a barrage of Elation damage by consuming skill points.

The new Ugreen Honkai: Star Rail collection is here with big launch discounts Final Fantasy 14: Evercold will revitalize the long-running MMO with all-new content and gameplay features — here are the top three things I can't wait to try Gambling, noir detectives, and urinating robots: Warframe's long-awaited Tau update is unlike anything I could possibly have predicted Of the two, I'm more drawn to Yao Guang, simply because we've seen how powerful supports can be throughout the lifecycle of Honkai Star Rail. Without a proper Elation damage dealer to go with her, though, she might be harder to fit into teams without a Sparxie at her side – but maybe patch 4.1 will help with that by providing more options.

The bright, vibrant and fantastical metropolis of Duomension City on Planarcadia. (Image credit: Hoyoverse) Here is the screen I will be looking at a lot over the next few months (Image credit: Hoyoverse) Sparxie can unleash some ridiculous attacks on enemies. (Image credit: Hoyoverse) Show off. (Image credit: Hoyoverse) Aha is the frivolous and tricksy Aeon at the centre of this update's story. (Image credit: Hoyoverse) Image 1 of 5 View Original

Of course, spending your saved up currency to get new characters is only part of the fun with a new update. Especially when it's a flagship update that's going to add a massive new planet named Planarcadia to explore.

You'll visit the vibrant metropolis of Duomension City with the main goal of entering the Phantasmoon Games, where the top prize is an audience with a god, and the chance to become an Aeon for one minute. I'm not deep into the Honkai Star Rail lore, but that sounds like a pretty powerful boon to me.

What gets my attention is one of the many new events coming in 4.0. Yes, I'm back on the CCG again. Named 'Cosmicon Collective', it seems you can go around the world, challenge others to unlock new cards, and build out your deck with characters, monsters and iconic figures from across the game. This is what I'm all about.

Other events revealed in today's livestream include a magazine management game (maybe a bit too much like a busman's holiday for me), a 2D side-scrolling platformer, which should be a fun change of pace from all the turn-based combat, and an expansion to the much-loved Currency Wars mode.
